name: R-11 revision-5 first 24-hour bg-host embedding window: INCONCLUSIVE
command: Read dbos.workflow_status rows for name='embedBackfill' in the missing interval; group by status and recovery_attempts, then bound additional sweep attempts by sum(1 + recovery_attempts)
Parse starts, exclusions, errorClass, and per-target completion counts as specified in method; compare with the committed baseline
summary: The first revision-5 24-hour window cannot be graded in full: its first 3h48m20s and the start-target snapshot are absent. DBOS records bound missing-interval sweep attempts, so the error-rate falsifier fires even if every missing sweep was eligible and error-free, provided this was the qualifying continuous-engine window. That continuity remains unproven; the exact full-window ratio is unknown and no pass is claimed.

window.coverageBasis: Both journalctl --list-boots and journalctl --user --list-boots begin with boot d02155aeac354b23898e7325f799da48 at 2026-10-02 00:41:49 EDT; journalctl --user returned zero lines for the missing interval. No full-window journal source was found.

runtime.continuousBuildCoverage: unknown because the start of the window has no retained journal

method.source: R-11 rubric revision 5; errorClass comes from r11-window-analysis.json
method.sweepBoundary: Each sweep starts at one [embed-backfill] sweep starting line and ends at the next such line or window end.
method.excludedSweeps: A sweep is excluded if it overlaps a sidecar Stopping/Starting event or contains a sidecar-reported database time-budget error.
method.parse: Parse the leading ISO timestamp and [embed-backfill] message from short-iso-precise journal lines. Count error-like messages only within eligible sweeps.

missingIntervalRateBound.source: Read-only dev:pg_query of dbos.workflow_status where name='embedBackfill' and created_at falls in this interval, measured 2026-10-03T01:22Z
missingIntervalRateBound.workflowStatus: All 45 rows have status SUCCESS; 43 have recovery_attempts=1 and 2 have recovery_attempts=2.
missingIntervalRateBound.boundMethod: Conservatively allow 1+recovery_attempts executions for each workflow row, and one logged sweep per execution. The bg-host source calls runEmbedBackfillOnce once in embedBackfillTick, which calls _runSweepLogged once; repository search found no other bg-host caller. This treats every possible missing attempt as an eligible zero-error sweep, minimizing the rate.
missingIntervalRateBound.comparison: 112/(205+92)=0.3771043771 > 74/266=0.2781954887. Therefore the rate falsifier fires if this is the qualifying window, even without the missing journal interval. The exact full-window numerator and denominator remain unknown.
missingIntervalRateBound.limitations: The bound assumes the retained DBOS workflow ledger is complete for this interval and the bg-host made no out-of-band sweep call. The surviving source and 5-minute DBOS schedule support those assumptions; the absent journal cannot verify them directly.

distinctObservedTemplates: a sweep has held the latch
formatStringCheck.result: all five templates occur in pre-extraction source; only the first three remain in eligible sweeps after rev5 exclusions

assertions.evidence: The first 13,700 seconds of the required window have no retained journal records.
Ten targets embedded rows in the observed portion, but there is no start-of-window missing-row snapshot, so the required proof is incomplete.
Every observed error-like template was found at 9a9473af95.

Conditional falsifier: even allowing 92 additional eligible zero-error sweeps, 112/(205+92)=0.3771043771 exceeds baseline 74/266=0.2781954887. Exact full-window counts and qualifying-window continuity remain unavailable.

limitations: No start-of-window per-target missing-row snapshot is available; aggregate embedding counts cannot prove that each row missing at the start was embedded.
The absent early-window sweeps prevent an exact full-window ratio, but the conservative DBOS bound places its minimum above baseline if this is the qualifying continuous-engine window.
Longer observed sweep durations accompany more budget-expired and latch-skip lines; this is correlation, not an established cause of the latency change.
